steps.text: Cook bacon in a skillet over medium heat until browned and crispy.
Pour bacon and grease into a heatproof bowl and allow to cool.
Heat oil in a skillet. Add shallots and garlic. Cook and stir until softened, about 3 minutes.
Mix venison with cooled bacon mixture. Season with Worcestershire sauce, parsley, salt, and pepper. Stir in egg until evenly combined. Refrigerate for 20 minutes.
Preheat an outdoor grill for medium-high heat.
Grill to desired doneness. Serve on toasted hamburger buns with your favorite toppings.

raw_recipe.headline: Venison Bacon Burgers
raw_recipe.description: An easy venison burger recipe. Crisp, crumbly bacon is mixed into seasoned ground venison to make the best juicy burgers you've ever tasted.
raw_recipe.name: Venison Bacon Burgers

review.reviewBody: We are always looking for ways to use our deer meat. We never grill burgers as they are always a little dry. Well, this recipe was awesome! My husband and kids loved these burgers! So moist and delicious. We will definitely have these again and again!!

This was wonderful!!!! This was my first time cooking ground venison, having made swiss style venison steaks. I had a little over 1lb so I divided all the ingredients close half. I cooked the 3 slices of bacon in the microwave, cut into pieces with scissors. Used yellow onion and Italian seasoning in place of parsley. I did use cast iron skillet and followed recommendation in Katie's review 201. However I got 3 burgers. The cooking times were perfect. I sautéed the garlic and onion in oil for 2 minutes. Her procedure follows. "Three minutes on each side in a medium heat preheated cast iron. Then put it in the oven (425 degrees) for 3-4 minutes. Perfect.

This is a great recipe. I ground my mule deer with a high quality grass fed chuck roast which added some fat and an overall larger yield. I also did about 10% beef suet so this burger with the added bacon is better than any restaurant burger. I cooked the bacon whole and then chopped it.

This was really good. We had never tried venison before but my husband got a deer this year. This city girl had no idea how to cook it. This is how. Soooo tasty even my five year old ate it. Hubs went back for seconds. And the leftovers reheated well the next day - not that there were many of them. I did it in a cast iron on the stove like several others commented they did. I got seven burgers out of my pound of meat, so I think I made them a little smaller than the recipe intended. Three minutes on each side in a medium heat preheated cast iron. Then put it in the oven (425 degrees) for 3-4 minutes. Perfect.

Delicious!! I just recently discovered venison and absolutely love it. I had 12 oz of ground venison so I used 3 slices nitrate-free bacon, red onion and fresh garlic instead of the shallots. I added a bit of butter to the pan after I cooked the bacon and sweated the onion and garlic. I used half a beaten egg and some panko bread crumbs too because my meat seemed a bit sticky. I also added some dried thyme based on another recipe I read on this site. The pan looked too good with all the brown bits and bacon grease/butter so I added a bit of olive oil and seared the burgers that way. Just have to keep a close eye on the heat because they cook quickly..about 4 mins on each side was maximum to still get 3 juicy burgers. Added some sliced provolone on top..a nice mild cheese to counter the meaty flavors was perfect. Loved the smokiness of the bacon, the freshness of the parsley and the beautifully different flavor of venison. Ive seen so many recipes with reviews that state all the tricks they used to mask the flavor of the venison. If you have to mask it..you probably just don't enjoy eating it lol. This recipe was great..thanks so much for sharing it!

yes, will make it again! according to another reviewer's advice, i soaked the raw ground deer (he said in water but i usually soak my venison in milk. Soaking venison in milk or water helps drain blood out of the meat so it tastes more mellow. Since i was grilling it and didn't want to worry about it burning quickly, i soaked it in unsweetened almond milk). let it soak in bowl in the fridge about a half hour then i drained the meat and squeezed handfuls of it to get out the milk. then i followed the recipe. quick tip***cut the raw bacon up with scissors before cooking it. it cooks quicker and no need to crumble it cuz it is already chopped***.tripled the amount of fresh parsley. DOES NOT NEED ADDED SALT,THE BACON IS SALTY ENOUGH!
I used a black peppered bacon so no need to add additional black pepper. we like a lot of garlic so i just kept spooning more from the jar of minced garlic that i keep on hand. served them with provolone and swiss cheese. THESE HAD NO GAMEY TASTE WHATSOEVER. i actually was a little disappointed because i like a little gamey tast. so next time, i will not soak the venison in milk before i mix up the recipe. another thing i wanna do next time is chop mushroom and mix into the patty, or just serve them with sauteed mushrooms. The best part of this recipe was that it was absolutely moist and delicious, not dry at all. All that bacon and grease did not make it greasy or overpowering at all. Actually, because we did grill the patties over charcoal

This was my first ever attempt at venison and I was very happy with the result. Out of necessity, I made some adjustments to the recipe. I had to add about a pound of ground beef (80/20) to the pound of venison I was given. I soaked the venison in milk for several hours, just wanting to make sure these wouldn't be too gamey and touch. Instead they were moist and delicious.

These were great, moist and flavorful! I took out the shallots and ended cooking a little early so I could broil the patties with a slice of cheddar on top for a minute. I used a whole egg for just 2 burgers, which was a bit much, but it kept everything moist for cooking. Next time I'll add some spice for a little something extra.

This recipe makes a very good burger. I did not have shallots on hand so I used onion, otherwise stuck pretty close to the recipe. It helps to keep the burgers held together if frozen first. Also, a well oiled grate and cooking at a lower temperature for a longer period of time works well. For best results, never cook venison beyond medium rare.

Soo good! I didn’t have shallots on hand but instead used a small diced up sweet onion. Kind of eye- balled the rest of the ingredients but you really can’t go wrong with the base of this recipe! I used my air-fryer instead though and cooked three at a time for 10 mins! Super juicy and tasty. Will definitely be my go-to recipe for a quick burger night.

AWESOME!!! My family (especially my wife) has gone from dreading me cooking with venison, to asking if we can harvest more venison next year. The way I prepare the meat ensures there is absolutely NO gamey taste. I thaw the burger completely at room temp and then allow it to soak in cold water for at least an hour to allow the blood to drain from the meat. The dark color leaves and it looks alot like hamburger. I have also prepared the burger with just the bacon, bacon grease, cooked onion, and garlic, and used it in my meatloaf recipe. Also great! We now try to stock our freezer with vension during the season.

This recipe is awesome. The venison cheeseburger tasted so good. I'm definitely going to recommend this to friends who have deer meat. I followed the recipe except I had dry parsley. I did cook the burger in a cast iron frying pan then put it in the oven as was recommended in one of the comments. "Three minutes on each side in a medium heat preheated cast iron. Then put it in the oven (425 degrees) for 3-4 minutes. Perfect.

Hubby came across this recipe last month and made this for dinner to use up our ground venison meat. Oohh my freaking goodness!!!! He’s not allowed to make any other kind of burgers BUT THESE from now on! We’re making these bad boys again for dinner tomorrow. Absolutely love this recipe. Thank you for sharing this delicious recipe.
One of the best burgers I've ever made! I used one lb instead of two. Im still shocked.

For the record: I’ve never had a venison burger that I liked. My kids don’t have a lot of experience with game meat beyond some novelties. I gave this recipe a try and even the picky child cleaned up her plate. If you have some leftover venison in the freezer, I highly recommend these Deerburgers. Pros: Zero game taste. Con: Be careful on the grill. That bacon grease is trying to get out and is susceptible to big flare ups.
This is the best burger ever!
Our go-to deer burger recipe! Everyone loves it!!
Better than beef burger!
I used onion instead of shallots and doubled the garlic. Smoked/grilled over mesquite. I also used dried parsley; the parsley was present but fresh would have been much better. These are fantastic!
AMAZE BALLS!!!! Really ... that’s all I can say. I followed the recipe exactly and we devoured every bite . Hands down the BEST venison burger I have ever made or tasted. AMAZE BALLS!!!
